Vault (external secret store)

Optionally keep appliance passwords, directory secrets and integration-hook secrets in an external OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault (KV v2) instead of, or in addition to, the local encrypted database — and migrate or remove the local copies safely.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → Access & Identity → Vault (URL /settings/#tab-vault)

  • Advanced

What is it?#

By default every credential SATOM holds — appliance passwords, the directory bind password, the FortiAuthenticator shared secret, integration-hook secrets — is encrypted with a local key and stored in SATOM's database. The Vault tab adds an external OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault (KV v2 API) so the key material no longer sits on the same host as the data it protects. Nothing changes until you turn it on: Store in SATOM only remains the default.

What does it do?#

  • Three storage modes for new secrets:
  • Store in SATOM only (Fernet) — default; the vault is not used.
  • Store in both — read vault first, fall back to SATOM — migration mode; nothing breaks if the vault is down, but the local copy still exists.
  • Store in the vault only — closes the exposure; a vault outage makes credentials unavailable.
  • Test connection — checks reachability, seal state, authentication and mount access.
  • Migrate existing credentials — copies every stored appliance password, the RADIUS shared secret, the LDAP/AD bind password, the alert webhook signing secret (to alerts/webhook) and every integration-hook secret (to hooks/<NAME>) into the vault, reading each back to confirm. Remove the local copies covers the same set.
  • Remove the local copies — replaces each local copy with a marker once the vault is confirmed to hold the identical value. Irreversible; only in vault-only mode.

Requirements#

  • users.manage.
  • A KV v2 mount on the vault and either an AppRole (role_id + secret_id) or a static token with read/write access to it.
  • The vault's TLS certificate trusted by the node (system trust store or the CA certificate field).

Permissions#

🔑Permission

All four endpoints (POST /settings/vault, /vault/test, /vault/migrate, /vault/scrub) require users.manage. Without it the Access & Identity group is hidden and calls return 403.

How to use#

  1. 1ConfigureAddress, mount, AppRole or token; Save
  2. 2TestTest connection must report the mount readable
  3. 3MirrorMode "Store in both", enable, Save
  4. 4MigrateDry run, then Copy to vault — every item verified
  5. 5Vault onlyMode "Store in the vault only", Save
  6. 6ScrubDry run, then Remove local copies
  1. Open Settings → Access & Identity → Vault.
  2. Fill Vault address, KV v2 mount, Authentication and its credentials, then click Save (leave Use an external vault off for now if you only want to test).
  3. Click Test connection. The Status card shows ✓ Vault &lt;version&gt; reachable, unsealed, mount 'satom' readable. (plus the token's policies) or a ✗ with the reason.
  4. Switch on Use an external vault, choose Store in both — read vault first, fall back to SATOM and Save — "Vault settings saved."
  5. In Migrate existing credentials, click Dry run, review the list, then Copy to vault and confirm "Copy every stored credential into the vault?". The summary reads N copied, N skipped, N failed.
  6. When everything is copied, choose Store in the vault only and Save. The flash warns: "Vault saved. The vault is now the ONLY store for new secrets — existing local copies are untouched until you migrate."
  7. In Remove the local copies, click Dry run, then Remove local copies and confirm "Remove every local copy that the vault already holds? This cannot be undone."

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Use an external vault Master switch. Cannot be saved ON without an address. Default off. No on
Where new secrets are written One of the three modes above. Default Store in SATOM only (Fernet). No Store in both
Vault address Base URL; a trailing / is removed. Must be an http:// or https:// URL: any other scheme (for example file://) is refused on every vault request. When enabled https://vault.example.com:8200
KV v2 mount Mount path. Default satom. No satom
Authentication AppRole (default) or Static token. Yes AppRole
Namespace (optional) Vault Enterprise / OpenBao namespace. No ops
AppRole role_id Used with AppRole. AppRole 1a2b…
AppRole secret_id Stored encrypted, never shown; blank keeps the current one. AppRole —
Static token Stored encrypted, never shown; only used with Static token; blank keeps the current one. Token —
Timeout (s) Request timeout, 1–120, default 10. No 10
Verify the vault TLS certificate Default on. Turning it off is not a substitute for a CA: every appliance password crosses this connection. No on
CA certificate (PEM, or a path on this node) Blank = system trust store. No PEM text

The Status card shows enabled/disabled, the mode, and configured (address plus complete credentials for the chosen authentication) or incomplete.

Example#

🧪Example — Move to vault-only without downtime

Run the flow on a quiet afternoon. Because Store in both reads the vault first and falls back to the local copy, a vault hiccup during migration cannot take appliances offline. Only after Copy to vault reports 0 failed switch to Store in the vault only, then scrub.

Result#

  • Configuration is stored in app_settings (secrets encrypted); audit entries settings.vault, settings.vault_migrate (copied/failed) and settings.vault_scrub (scrubbed/failed). Dry runs are not audited.
  • In mirror and vault-only modes, appliance passwords, the RADIUS shared secret and integration-hook secrets saved in the console are written to the vault; in vault-only mode the local column receives only a marker. Script Library credentials are vault-only in every mode.
  • In Store in both, a secret saved while the vault could not be written keeps its new value in SATOM, and its vault path is marked as stale: until a write succeeds, SATOM reads its own copy for it instead of the older vault copy. Test connection lists stale paths; Copy to vault (Migrate existing credentials) rewrites them and clears the mark.

Troubleshooting#

"A vault address is required before enabling the vault."#

Solution — fill Vault address, then save with the switch on.

"The vault is not configured yet."#

Possible causes — Migrate was run before an address and complete credentials were saved.

Solution — complete and Save the form; the Status badge must read configured.

"The vault is not the authoritative store. Set the mode to “Store in the vault only” before removing local copies."#

Solution — finish migration, switch the mode to vault-only and save, then run the scrub.

Test reports "Unreachable: the vault address must be an http(s) URL (got '…')"#

Possible causes — Vault address uses a scheme other than http or https. The address is saved as typed; the check runs on every request SATOM sends to the vault, so the vault stays unusable until it is corrected.

Solution — enter the address as https://<host>:8200 (or http:// for a lab vault), save and click Test connection again.

Test reports "The vault is reachable but SEALED — it cannot answer for secrets."#

Solution — unseal the vault, then test again.

Test reports "Reachable, but authentication failed: …" or "Authenticated, but mount '…' is not readable: …"#

Solution — check the role_id/secret_id or token and that its policy grants access to the KV v2 mount; save and test again. Test connection uses the saved configuration.

A scrub item reports "no copy in the vault - the local one is the last one"#

Possible causes — that credential was never migrated or the vault copy differs. The local copy is kept on purpose.

Solution — run Copy to vault again, then repeat the scrub.

Advanced#

Advanced Paths, markers and caveats
  • When the vault owns a secret, the local column holds an encrypted marker instead of the password, so older code paths see a readable placeholder rather than an empty value.
  • Directory secrets live at auth/fortiauthenticator (field shared_secret) and auth/ldap (field bind_password) under the mount.
  • A new Bind password typed on Authentication is written to the vault and, unless the vault is the only store, to the local database too — the same path as the FortiAuthenticator shared secret — so sign-in, which reads the vault copy first, uses the new value. (Before 2.11.0 it was written only locally and the old vault copy kept being used.)
  • Saving the form invalidates the cached vault token.
